title: test/e2e: skip terminated build prune test for remote
body:
## Summary

Related to #28868.

The terminated-build prune test sends `SIGKILL` to the process running the build. In remote tests, that process is `podman-remote`, so killing it terminates the client while the server-side build may continue.

As a result, the remote version of this test does not exercise the same scenario as the local test, where `SIGKILL` terminates the actual build process.

## Changes

Skip `podman system prune --build clean up after terminated build` for remote runs using `SkipIfRemote()`.

The existing local coverage is unchanged.

This change is intentionally limited to the test behavior. It does not attempt to fix server-side build cancellation. The related prune race was handled separately in #29279, while remote build cancellation is being worked on in `containers/buildah#7007`.

## Validation

- `git diff --check`
- Successfully compiled the Linux ARM64 E2E test package with:

  ```console
  GOOS=linux GOARCH=arm64 CGO_ENABLED=0 go test -c -tags containers_image_openpgp ./test/e2e -o /tmp/podman-e2e.test

@Luap99 Thanks, agreed . After looking further into this, I don’t think skipping the remote case is the right approach since it would remove API/bindings coverage.
I traced the remote build path from the API handler into Buildah. With the currently vendored Buildah v1.45.0, the Dockerfile RUN path eventually starts the runtime subprocess without propagating the request context. Buildah #7007 changes this path to pass the stage context through RunContext() and use a context-aware subprocess.
I tested the existing podman system prune --build clean up after terminated build remote spec locally on Fedora CoreOS/aarch64 with both stock Buildah v1.45.0 and Buildah #7007. Both passed 10/10 runs, so I wasn’t able to reproduce the original CI flake locally and can’t claim #7007 fixes #28868 based on that test alone.
I’ll drop the skip approach. Would you prefer that I keep this PR open and update it once #7007 is merged/vendored, or should I investigate a more deterministic regression test for the remote cancellation path here?
I am closing this. We can keep the discussion on what to do in https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/28868
